editions.foundations_topic: Subthreshold swing and the 60 mV/decade limit
editions.headline: One power trace of ML-KEM key generation on a Cortex-M4 cuts the standardised post-quantum key exchange's estimated attack cost by more than 140 bits, and Vahid Jahandideh's 937-byte change to how the sampler stores a number restores nearly all of it.

A single-author preprint solves the supersingular one-endomorphism problem in p^(1/3) time and memory with no heuristic, turning the cost isogeny-based cryptography already assumed into one it can prove.

Orbital torque from a thick titanium/tungsten bilayer writes a magnetic memory bit on 300-millimetre wafers for under 0.1 picojoule, removing the few-nanometre spin source that has capped the technology.

DeepSeek's new Flash model holds a token's key-value cache in 890 bytes of high-bandwidth memory, about a quarter of its predecessor's, by sharing keys across layers and storing them in four-bit floating point.

A symbolic checker that examines one output location for every input, instead of every output for one input, found real bugs in 600 of 6,988 machine-written CUDA kernels that differential testing had already passed.

editions.foundations_topic: Depth of focus, and why the wafer has to be flat
editions.headline: A Twente–ASML team moved the top of a lithography wafer support pillar 9.3 nanometres using a 4.5-micrometre piezoelectric film beneath it, the first active substrate support built from thin films rather than bulk actuators, which is what makes thousands per clamp conceivable.

Chris S. Lin's group turned GPU Rowhammer from a handful of bit flips into 23,597 per bank on an Nvidia RTX A5000, and showed that triple-bit errors inside one 16-byte chunk alias past the card's error-correcting code as clean data.

Yu Liu and twenty-one co-authors halved the DRAM bit cell to 2F² by bonding a wafer face-down and building a second cell on its backside, and report 27.5 percent less parasitic load, 11 percent more sense margin and half the area against a 4F² baseline.

editions.foundations_topic: The von Neumann architecture and its bottleneck
editions.headline: Aalto University inverted a standing rule of atomic layer deposition: halving how much film each cycle leaves drove zinc oxide 45 percent deeper into a 2,000-to-1 channel at the same dose, because depth scales as the inverse square root of per-cycle uptake.

A quiet weekend in the stack, with no new preprint announcements since Friday: the sharpest result still standing is the Intern-NCP team's 8.9-billion-parameter latent-space model, which reaches OLMo-3-7B's final pretraining loss after 51.3 percent of the tokens.

editions.foundations_topic: CVD: LPCVD, PECVD, and the pressure trade
editions.headline: A four-author team reconstructed the arithmetic inside NVIDIA's cuBLAS well enough to match it bit for bit on Blackwell and Hopper, then built the first static checker that decides whether two GPU kernels sum in the same order across NVIDIA PTX and AMD GCN.

A six-author group shows that cooling a chip is enough to defeat the sensors meant to catch a halted clock: at −36 °C, OpenTitan's alert handler never escalates and the AES key is still sitting in its registers when the part warms up.

Apple's A20 Pro breaks with package-on-package: the iPhone 18 Pro's memory now sits beside the processor die instead of on top of it, leaving the die's upper face free to meet a vapour chamber with three times the previous surface area.

editions.foundations_topic: Resolution, NA, and the k₁ factor
editions.headline: A 149-test CUDA benchmark finds NVIDIA's Compute Sanitizer memcheck reports 18 of the 144 GPU memory-safety violations that apply to it, because its guard regions catch an overflow that lands in dead space and not one that runs into the next live allocation.

ASML and TSMC opened an industry programme to grow the photomask from six inches to twelve, because high-NA EUV's anamorphic optics cut the printed field from 26 × 33 mm to 26 × 16.5 mm and left the largest dies to be stitched from two exposures.

A University of Chicago-led group reports remote epitaxy on metallic and covalently bonded substrates, which a central belief in the field says should not work: the rule for which crystals can grow a peel-off single-crystal film stops being about ionic bonding.

editions.foundations_topic: ENIAC, EDVAC, and the stored-program idea
editions.headline: A quiet weekend in the stack, with no new preprint announcement since Friday and no standards release: the sharpest result standing is Rice University's Einsummable, which models every tensor operation as a relational join and beats hand-tuned PyTorch on an eight-GPU server.

editions.foundations_topic: OPC, phase-shift masks, and inverse lithography
editions.headline: Four researchers re-read 83 microarchitectural side-channel papers from 2014 to 2024 and found 92.8 percent carry at least one full evaluation flaw and 49.4 percent shipped no code, so a decade of attack numbers cannot be ranked against each other.

An ETH Zürich and Czech Academy of Sciences group shows one misplaced soft phonon is why first-principles electro-optic predictions run low: put the measured frequency back and potassium niobate lands at 374 pm/V against 360 ± 30 measured.

editions.foundations_topic: MEMS fabrication: surface versus bulk micromachining
editions.headline: The Optical Internetworking Forum approved CMIS-LT on 2 September: a switch chip and the optical module plugged into it can now negotiate transmitter equalisation over the management bus, instead of both running a setting fixed on a compliance board.

editions.foundations_topic: DRAM: the one-transistor cell, its capacitor, and refresh
editions.headline: DDR5's standardised RowHammer defence turns out to be an attack surface of its own: a paper for RTSS 2026 shows an attacker task priming per-row activation counters can stretch a victim's runtime to 200 percent of its certified worst case.

ASML put production numbers on high-NA EUV at SEMICON Taiwan: ten 0.55-NA scanners running at four customers, 135 wafers an hour at acceptance on an EXE:5200B, and 1.35 million wafers exposed across the fleet.

editions.foundations_topic: Thermal oxidation and the Deal–Grove model
editions.headline: A quiet two days at the end of August: the most consequential thing published is an EPFL circulator that gets 40 decibels of isolation out of ordinary 65-nanometre CMOS by making two leakage paths cancel.

Hot Chips week turned the memory package into the design problem: Samsung is moving the HBM base die to a 4 nm logic process, SK hynix says a 775-micrometre height limit caps the stack, and Intel dropped HBM for 480 GB of LPDDR5X.

The week's biggest numbers shrank on inspection: Applied Materials says cleanroom floor space, not capital, now gates chip capacity, and Nvidia's $105 billion for Ohio turns out to be a lease guaranty rather than financing.
